relationships.description: The joint behaviour carried out by the collaborating components produces the outcome that gives an externally offered application service its worth to consumers, such as a checkout saga delivering the completed-order result of an ordering service.
relationships.evidence: Service documentation or an API contract states that the service's operation outcome (e.g. order confirmed) is produced only when the saga or choreography completes, and the saga's final step returns or publishes that result.

relationships.description: The interaction can only run when the named grouping of components that jointly carries it out is in place, since no single participant can complete the saga, choreography or handshake alone.
relationships.evidence: A saga orchestrator definition, choreography spec or deployment manifest lists the participating services of the collaboration as required steps or participants of the interaction.

relationships.description: The interaction requires a specific state-change occurrence to start, advance or complete, such as a choreography step that waits for a PaymentCaptured event before continuing.
relationships.evidence: Participant code subscribes to the event's topic or queue (e.g. a Kafka listener or event handler registration) as a step of the saga, or the saga definition names the event as a trigger or transition.

relationships.description: The interaction calls on another application service's operations to complete one or more of its steps, so it cannot finish if that service is unavailable.
relationships.evidence: A saga step or choreography handler invokes the service's client, endpoint or RPC method, or the interaction's specification lists the service as a required dependency.

relationships.description: The interaction needs a particular data structure to carry state between its participants, such as the message payload or saga state record exchanged across the handshake.
relationships.evidence: The saga state class, message schema or payload type is imported and serialized/deserialized by the participants' interaction handlers, or declared in the protocol's schema definitions.

relationships.description: The collaborative behaviour is the concrete mechanism through which the externally visible application service is actually delivered, with the service's operations implemented by the saga or multi-party exchange.
relationships.evidence: The service's API endpoint or operation handler starts the saga or choreography and returns its result, or architecture documentation maps the service operation to the interaction as its implementation.

notes: delivers-value to ApplicationService is redundant with realizes and misuses a traceability predicate meant for business value/goals. depends-on ApplicationCollaboration inverts ArchiMate semantics: the collaboration should be assigned-to the interaction. depends-on DataObject would be more precise as accesses.
